governed_construct: Each typed position in a TypeScript file: a variable, parameter, property, index signature, function/method return, type assertion, type argument or type-parameter default, whether its type is written explicitly or inferred by the checker. One instance = one such declaration or type position.
interpretation: The rule forbids the `any` type, whether written (`: any`, `any[]`, `Record<string, any>`, `as any`, `<T = any>`) or silently inferred: a binding whose type the checker resolves to `any` (e.g. `const x = JSON.parse(s)`, `const body = await res.json()`) uses the any type just as much and is a violation, because the rule's remedy is to annotate such values as `unknown`. A unit conforms when every declaration/type position resolves to a type that neither is nor contains `any`; `unknown` with narrowing, generics and concrete types conform. The word `any` in comments or strings is irrelevant. A file with no declarations or type positions at all (only top-level expression statements) is NOT_APPLICABLE. Because inferred `any` has no `AnyKeyword` node, detection needs the type checker, hence T3.
